subject: Pathology Markers
title: Cardiac Biomarkers: Kinetics & Relapse Detection
preview: Interpret cardiac troponin using serial measurements, a validated assay and the clinical/ECG picture, rather than a universal timing chart.

sections.title: Troponin: injury is not always infarction
points: Consider symptoms, electrocardiographic evidence, imaging and other causes of troponin elevation.
Myocarditis, renal dysfunction, severe illness and tachyarrhythmias can accompany troponin elevation without plaque rupture.

sections.title: Use assay-specific serial testing
points: Interpret baseline and repeat high-sensitivity troponin under the validated local diagnostic pathway.
Recurrent symptoms after a recent infarction require clinical assessment, repeat ECG and selected serial biomarkers, not a single rigid timeline.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A normal early measurement does not always exclude an acute evolving coronary syndrome.
CK-MB is not generally the preferred modern biomarker when validated cardiac troponin testing is available.

quickRevision: Myocardial injury is defined by elevated cardiac troponin; acute injury is suggested by a rise or fall on serial testing.
Myocardial infarction additionally requires evidence of acute myocardial ischemia; troponin elevation alone does not establish an infarction.
High-sensitivity assays have laboratory-specific thresholds and testing intervals; do not apply a universal cutoff.

quiz.question: What does an elevated cardiac troponin indicate most directly?
options: Definite plaque rupture in every case
A specific coronary artery in all cases
quiz.explanation: Elevated cardiac troponin identifies myocardial injury; infarction additionally needs evidence of ischemia and serial interpretation of the clinical picture.
